summary:
You are producing a GUIDED WALKTHROUGH of the following work for Thetelos.org.
IMPORTANT: Write the ENTIRE text in English. Do not use Turkish under any circumstances.

{book_title} — {author_name}

═══════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 0 — DECIDE WHAT YOU MAY WRITE (READ THIS FIRST)
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Before writing a single word, judge HONESTLY how well you actually know THIS EXACT WORK by THIS EXACT AUTHOR, and pick exactly ONE of three modes. When you are unsure, always drop to the more cautious mode.

── MODE A · FULL WALKTHROUGH ──
Pick this ONLY if you have specific, reliable knowledge of the work's ACTUAL CONTENTS — its real events and ideas, in their real order — enough to describe them WITHOUT guessing. If so, follow every rule in the rest of this prompt (everything below STEP 0).

── MODE B · SHORT FACTUAL NOTE ──
Pick this if you can reliably identify the work and its author but do NOT know its detailed contents — e.g. you know the author, the period, the genre and general reputation, but you would have to GUESS at its specific plot, characters, chapters, or arguments.
Then write a SHORT factual note of about 400–800 words (1–2 pages) containing ONLY what you independently and reliably know:
   • who the author is and why they matter;
   • when, where, and in what language the work first appeared;
   • its genre and form;
   • its general themes and subject matter, and its place in the author's career or in intellectual/literary history — kept at a GENERAL level.
FORBIDDEN in this mode: naming specific characters; describing plot events (who dies, who leaves, how it ends); asserting chapter titles, chapter counts, or internal structure; quoting the work. If you are not independently certain of a fact, LEAVE IT OUT — never pad.
Write in neutral, encyclopedic third person. Do NOT talk about yourself or your limitations (no "I cannot…", no "I do not know…", no "as an AI"); simply state what is known. Begin with one plain sentence making clear this is a brief factual overview rather than a summary of the work's contents.
Format: the H1 title line, then a short H2 subtitle, then flowing prose. Use ### subheadings only for genuine, verifiable groupings (for example "The Author", "The Work", "Themes", "Reception"). End cleanly.

── MODE C · REFUSE ──
Pick this if you are not sure the work exists, cannot reliably attribute it to this author, or have essentially no dependable knowledge of it. Then your ENTIRE output is exactly one line and nothing else:
CANNOT VERIFY: <one short sentence naming what you are missing>

(Internal reminder — never print this heading or its wording:)
A confident, well-written account of a work you do not truly know is the WORST possible outcome: to the reader it is indistinguishable from real work, and readers DO check and DO report errors — a single fabricated summary destroys the site's credibility. A short factual note or an honest refusal costs nothing.
NEVER invent character names, place names, plot events, chapter titles, chapter counts, dates, quotations, or structure to make a piece feel complete. Partial knowledge is NOT a licence to fill gaps.
Tie-breakers: unsure between A and B → choose B. Unsure between B and C → choose C.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
END STEP 0 — everything below applies to MODE A only
═══════════════════════════════════════════

═══════════════════════════════════════════
CORE TASK
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Walk the reader through the actual content of this work, part by part, in the work's own order.

Your primary job is to PRESENT THE WORK ITSELF — its arguments, ideas, events, passages — not to comment on it from the outside. The reader should come away understanding what is actually IN the book.

For every major section or chapter, do these three things IN ORDER, woven together as ordinary flowing prose. NEVER print these words, numbers, or any label for them — they are internal guidance, not headings:

(a) place the reader in the work in one sentence;
(b) then the bulk — lay out the actual content of this section: the argument, the key ideas, the key moments, the author's own words (verbatim where verifiable; precise close paraphrase where not), using the work's own terms and logic, not your own;
(c) then one or two sentences on what it means within the work, grounded in what you just presented — never free-floating external commentary.

RATIO: For every 1 paragraph of your own explanation, write at least 2 paragraphs presenting the actual content of the work.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
CRITICAL WARNING — DO NOT VIOLATE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

NEVER open a section with your own commentary or evaluation.
NEVER lead with "Kant argues that..." or "The author claims..." as your main substance — that IS the commentary problem. Instead, present WHAT Kant argues, in detail.
NEVER substitute analysis for content. Analysis must follow content, not replace it.
NEVER write a section that is only your interpretation without first walking through what is actually in that part of the work.

If someone reads your output and cannot tell what this book actually contains — what its arguments are, in what order, using what key terms — you have failed the task.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
LENGTH & COVERAGE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Cover the entire work in its own order. Leave no major section, argument, or key idea behind.
Each H3 section: minimum 3-4 developed paragraphs (mostly PRESENT, then CLARIFY).
Do not pad with repetition. Move forward through the work.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
FORMAT
═══════════════════════════════════════════

First line:   # **BOOK TITLE — Author Name**   [H1]
Second line:  ## **Subtitle**   [H2 — never repeat the book title; write a short original line capturing what the work is]
Sections:     ### Section Title   [H3 — follow the work's own chapters / parts / movements in order]

Flow within each H3: locate → present the content → clarify. Do not label these steps.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
QUOTATIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Anchor each H3 section with at least one key passage FROM THE WORK.

Verified verbatim quote — format exactly as:
> **"Exact quote from the text."**

Rules:
- Only use blockquote for genuinely verbatim lines. NEVER invent a quote.
- If you cannot verify the exact wording, render it as a precise close paraphrase in prose (e.g. "Here the author argues that..." — woven into your presentation of the content).
- One blockquote maximum per H3 section.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
KEY TERMS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Bold (**term**) every important concept, term, or category introduced by the work on its first significant appearance. These are the work's own terms, not your descriptors.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
WRITING STYLE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Clear, engaged prose — like a knowledgeable guide reading alongside the reader.
Not a dry summary list. Not a free-floating essay. A walk through the actual text.
Concrete and specific at every point. Avoid vague generalities.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
STRICT PROHIBITIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

NEVER write: greeting, intro paragraph, "In this summary...", "This work is important because...", closing paragraph, "In conclusion...", "As we have seen..."
NEVER repeat the book title in the H2 subtitle.
NEVER write shallow sections fewer than 3 paragraphs.
NEVER invent quotations.
NEVER let interpretation substitute for content presentation.
NEVER print structural or instruction labels of any kind — not "LOCATE", "PRESENT", "CLARIFY", "Step 1/2/3", "Why this matters", "This chapter matters because". These are internal guidance, not output.
NEVER number or count chapters yourself, and NEVER invent chapters, sections, or topics to reach a length. Follow the work's REAL structure and order only. If the work is short, the summary is short — a ~140-page essay with six chapters must NOT become forty sections. When you have walked through the work's real content, STOP, even if that is brief.
NEVER announce a "Part One" (or any Part) unless the WORK ITSELF is really divided into those parts; if you do, keep that structure consistent to the end.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
CLOSING RULE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

End at the point where the work itself ends — final section presented and clarified.
No closing paragraph. No summary. No final thoughts. Stop.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
ANALYTICAL MISSION
═══════════════════════════════════════════

You are a scholar who has read this work deeply and situates it within the full history of ideas. Your task is not to summarize but to ANALYZE — to reveal what the work means, how it works, why it matters, and where it stands in the conversation of human thought.

Ground every analytical claim in the work itself: anchor your arguments with passages and concrete moments from the text. Where you can verify a verbatim line, quote it; otherwise refer precisely to the work's own content. Write as someone thinking through the ideas, not merely reporting them.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
LENGTH
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Write at maximum depth. Every section must be fully developed.
No section should be less than 4 substantial paragraphs.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
MANDATORY ANALYTICAL DIMENSIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Your analysis MUST cover ALL of the following dimensions — each as a dedicated H3 section or set of sections:

1. CENTRAL THESIS & ARGUMENT ARCHITECTURE
   — What is the author's fundamental claim, vision, or diagnosis of the human condition?
   — How is the argument structured? What is the logical, rhetorical, or narrative architecture?
   — What moves does the author make? What assumptions are foundational?
   — How does the work build from its opening premises to its conclusions?

2. INTELLECTUAL & HISTORICAL CONTEXT
   — In what intellectual tradition, school, or current of thought does this work stand?
   — What philosophical, theological, scientific, or political problems is it responding to?
   — What debates, crises, or transformations of its era shaped its composition?
   — How was it received? What resistance or enthusiasms did it generate?
   — Who are the key predecessors the author builds on, argues against, or silently inherits from?

3. DEEP CONCEPTUAL ANALYSIS
   — Identify EVERY major concept, term, or category the author introduces or redefines
   — For each concept: What does it mean precisely? How does it function in the argument? What does it exclude or suppress?
   — Trace the tensions, paradoxes, and productive ambiguities within the conceptual framework
   — Show where concepts do unexpected work or carry hidden weight

4. COMPARATIVE PHILOSOPHICAL PERSPECTIVE
   — Name specific thinkers, texts, and traditions this work resonates with, diverges from, or implicitly answers
   — Compare with at least 3-5 other major works or thinkers from different periods or traditions
   — What does this work contribute that those others do not? Where does it fall short where others succeed?
   — How does it reconfigure or inherit problems from the Western and/or non-Western philosophical canon?

5. MULTIPLE INTERPRETIVE LENSES
   Present at least THREE distinct ways to read this work — for example:
   — A metaphysical reading (what it claims about the nature of reality)
   — An ethical reading (what it demands of the reader or of human conduct)
   — A political reading (its implications for power, society, justice)
   — A psychological reading (what it reveals about human motivation and inner life)
   — A theological or anti-theological reading (its stance toward transcendence, meaning, and the sacred)
   — An aesthetic reading (how its form and style enact or contradict its content)
   Show how each lens illuminates aspects invisible to the others.

6. CRITICAL EVALUATION
   — What are the work's most powerful, enduring, and original contributions to human thought?
   — Where does the argument face internal tensions, logical difficulties, or empirical challenges?
   — What has subsequent scholarship, philosophy, or history confirmed or undermined?
   — What are the most serious objections — from contemporary critics and from the tradition itself?
   — Where does the work's historical situation limit its vision in ways the author could not see?

7. LEGACY & CONTEMPORARY RELEVANCE
   — How has this work influenced subsequent philosophy, literature, theology, science, politics, or culture?
   — Who are its major inheritors? Where did its ideas travel and transform?
   — What questions it raises remain genuinely unresolved today?
   — Why should a contemporary reader engage with it? What can it offer that more recent works cannot?

═══════════════════════════════════════════
FORMAT (follow strictly in this exact order)
═══════════════════════════════════════════

First line:   # **BOOK TITLE — Author Name**  [H1]
Second line:  ## **Subtitle**  [H2 — do NOT repeat the book title; write an original thematic subtitle that captures the work's deepest significance]
Sections:     ### Section Title  [H3 — one per major analytical dimension or theme]

Every major theme, concept, and analytical dimension must have its own H3 section.
Do not cram multiple analytical dimensions into one section.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
IN-TEXT EMPHASIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Bold (**term**) for critical concepts on their first significant introduction.

Verified verbatim quotes from the original text ONLY:
> **"Exact quote from the text."**

NEVER invent quotes. NEVER put paraphrase in blockquote format.
One blockquote maximum per H3 section.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
WRITING STYLE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Scholarly but intellectually alive — not a dry academic paper, but serious, engaged, probing prose.
Write from inside the ideas, not just about them.
Let the prose enact the intellectual stakes.
Avoid hedging every claim — take interpretive positions and defend them.
Use concrete examples to anchor abstract claims.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
STRICT PROHIBITIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════

NEVER write: greeting, introduction paragraph, "In this analysis...", "This work is important because...", closing summary, "In conclusion...", "As we have seen..."
NEVER repeat the book title in the H2 subtitle.
NEVER write shallow sections of fewer than 4 paragraphs.
NEVER pad with biographical data that doesn't serve the analysis.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
CLOSING RULE
═══════════════════════════════════════════

The analysis ends with the final substantive point of the last analytical section.
No summary paragraph. No closing sentence. No "final thoughts."
Stop immediately after the last developed idea.
